sentences.text: Uronautes was a short-necked plesiosaur, a marine reptile closely related to other rhomaleosaurids.
Its neck vertebrae were notably short, possessing partially attached processes and double-headed ribs.
The name Uronautes combines Greek words meaning 'tailed' and 'sailor' or 'mariner'.
The genus was first described by the American paleontologist Edward Drinker Cope in 1876.
This animal belongs to the class Reptilia and the parent group Plesiosauria.
The type species of the genus is Uronautes cetiformis, the specimen the species is based on.
Uronautes lived during the Late Cretaceous period in the United States.
